newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta stable versus mark, trading range seen.
newsitem.headline: Peseta stable versus mark, trading range seen.

text.p: The peseta was trading virtually unchanged versus the mark on Tuesday morning after French President Chirac called early election as expected.
Dealers were expecting the peseta to move in a range trading between 84.40 and 84.65 per mark.
"We'll follow the dollar strictly. I guess the peseta can strengthen a bit in the morning if the dollar stops sliding," a dealer said.
But he added that another fall was possible later in the afternoon.
"Short term we'll depend more on the U.S. dollar and on the French franc, than on the France's election," said a forex dealer in Madrid.
At 0715 GMT, the peseta was trading at around 84.54/57 per mark versus an opening level at around 84.58/61 and 84.55/58 at the close on Monday.
Earlier on Tuesday Bundesbank Vice-President Johann-Wilhelm Gaddum said that starting the EMU with fewer members was not a problem.
"Gaddum's remarks could scare the market," a forex dealer in Madrid said, "fresh EMU jitters could push the peseta toward 85 per mark".
But he said if the peseta should break the 84.70 per mark level he was expecting the Bank of Spain to start defending its currency, selling marks.
French President Jacques Chirac announced on Monday evening he was dissolving the National Assembly and called an early parliamentary election for May 25 and June 1.
"After the initial uncertainty, dealers realized that it's likely that Chirac would win," another dealer added.

"The markets know that Chirac is an old hand in politics and would not call an election unless he thought he was going to win, but I'm sure there won't be any open bets on it as the polls have proved to be unreliable in recent elections," said Alfredo Urrutia, chief economist at Societe General in Madrid.
